title: Palm Sunday procession
hookLine: crowds with palms, in some places olive or willow branches

cards: A coat lands in the dust of the road. Then another. A man is coming toward Jerusalem on a young donkey, with people ahead of him and behind him, all shouting the same line.
Mark says some spread their garments in the way and others cut branches off the trees. John says they were palm branches. On Palm Sunday, churches walk that road again.

People gather outside, branches are blessed, and the whole congregation walks in together, carrying whatever grows near them: palms, and in some places olive or willow. Today, the Palm Sunday procession.

teach.b: Start with the shout, because the crowd didn't make it up. Matthew gives it like this in the King James: "Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest."

That middle line comes straight from Psalm 118, a song of thanks sung by someone arriving at the gates of the house of the Lord. The crowd reaches for words they know by heart and hands them to the man on the donkey.

teach.h: LOWLY, AND RIDING UPON AN ASS.
teach.b: Matthew says this happened to fulfil a word of the prophet, and in Zechariah it reads: "behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass."
A king, but not on a war horse, and not with an army. Lowly. Some readers hear the whole scene as Jesus showing what kind of king he means to be.
Now the branches. Only John names palms; Mark just says branches cut off the trees. The churches don't agree on one plant either.
Where palms grow, people carry palms; where they don't, they carry what's at hand. The point was never the species. It was a crowd laying something down in the road for someone they hoped in.
And here's the turn some churches keep on purpose.

teach.h: CHEERS AND THE CROSS, ONE SERVICE.
teach.b: The same service that opens with branches and singing goes on to read the whole story of the arrest and the cross. The cheering and the crying out happen in one service, as they happened in one week.
The road in leads to Friday.

how: On Palm Sunday, congregations that keep the procession gather outside, have branches blessed, and process into church singing; in some churches the service then reads the Passion, the story of Jesus's arrest and death.

o: a Hebrew word for king, used to crown Jesus
a palm branch waved in a festival parade

games.q: you're in the crowd as he rides by. you didn't bring a branch. what do you put on the road?
o: a sign with his name on it.
games.why: Mark says many spread their garments in the way, and others cut branches. people laid down what they had on them.

practice: Hold a branch or a leaf, a sprig from outside, a leaf from a houseplant, or rest one hand open as if you held one, and feel how light it is.
If you pray, say the crowd's line, blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; if not, think of what you would lay down for someone you honor.

wordCard.voice: Hosanna. The crowd's shout for Jesus riding into Jerusalem on a donkey, borrowed from Psalm 118 and carried into the church's Palm Sunday procession.

orig.note: Greek: blessed — the crowd's word in Matthew 21:9, "blessed is he that cometh."

carryVoice: Your line: blessed is he who comes. A psalm, shouted on the road. Back tomorrow, same hill.
